title: BODE Index (COPD Prognosis)
purpose: A multidimensional index (Body-mass index, airflow Obstruction, Dyspnoea, Exercise capacity) that predicts all-cause and respiratory mortality in COPD better than FEV1 alone. Used to time pulmonary rehabilitation, escalate therapy, and trigger lung transplant / palliative-care referral discussions. This is an outpatient/chronic-care tool — not for acute exacerbation triage.

options.label: 2 — walks slower than peers, or stops for breath walking at own pace
3 — stops for breath after ~100 m or a few minutes on the level
4 — too breathless to leave the house / breathless dressing

interpretation.label: Quartile 1 — approx. 80% 4-year survival. Optimise inhaler therapy, smoking cessation, vaccination, pulmonary rehab
Quartile 2 — approx. 67% 4-year survival. Ensure pulmonary rehab, review for LAMA/LABA/ICS escalation, treat comorbidities, assess for hypoxaemia (ambulatory + resting)
Quartile 3 — approx. 57% 4-year survival. Consider referral for advanced therapies (lung volume reduction, transplant evaluation if criteria met), advance-care planning
Quartile 4 — approx. 18% 4-year survival. Transplant evaluation if a candidate; integrate palliative care, discuss goals of care and NIV preferences, opioids for refractory dyspnoea

notes: A BODE rise after an exacerbation predicts worse outcome. The updated BODE (uses exacerbation frequency) and the ADO index (Age, Dyspnoea, Obstruction) are alternatives when a 6-minute walk is not feasible. GOLD ABE grouping guides pharmacotherapy; BODE guides prognosis and referral.
buildNote: Additive, 4 domains. Range 0–10, grouped into survival quartiles.
